text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. The main goal is to make your code readable, not just for the computer, but for other humans. One of the first steps is to choose clear naming conventions. A variable called `totalPrice` is far more understandable than `x` or `temp`. Similarly, a function named `calculateDiscount()` tells you exactly what it does. Instead of writing one long block of code, break it down into small, focused functions. Each function should do one single thing well. This approach greatly improves maintainability—when a bug appears, you can find it quickly, and when a feature needs to change, you only edit a small part of the whole. In short, always write code as if the next person to read it is a clever but sometimes impatient colleague.
